facts.statement: Thiesoscyllium is a newly described genus of carpet shark that includes two new species.
facts.quote:
Name: Thiesoscyllium
Novelty: Gen. et 2 sp. nov

facts.statement: The genus Thiesoscyllium is considered valid.
Fossils of Thiesoscyllium come from the Jurassic Toarcian to Bajocian ages.
Thiesoscyllium fossils have been found in Belgium and Luxembourg.
The type species of the genus is Thiesoscyllium underwoodi, and the genus also includes Thiesoscyllium felteni.
facts.quote: The type species is T. underwoodi; genus also includes T. felteni.

facts.statement: Thiesoscyllium is probably a member of the carpet shark family Hemiscylliidae.
facts.quote: A carpet shark, probably a member of the family Hemiscylliidae.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists Thiesoscyllium as a genus described by Delsate in 2026.
Thiesoscyllium belongs to the family Hemiscylliidae within the class Chondrichthyes.
Thiesoscyllium lived between 182.9 and 168.6 million years ago, spanning the Toarcian to Bajocian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Bajocian (182.9 to 168.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Three fossil occurrences of Thiesoscyllium have been recorded in the database.

rejected.statement: Thiesoscyllium was described by Delsate in 2026.
